claims.text: 3D ink extrusion printing, hydrogen de-binding, vacuum sintering at 1400°C for 18 hours with a titanium oxygen getter, and water quenching will improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The hydride-containing feedstock undergoes sequential hydride decomposition in the order Ta, Nb, then Hf/Ti/Zr.
Differences in hydride formation enthalpy cause the proposed decomposition sequence.
Sequential hydride decomposition facilitates in situ alloying.
Sequential hydride decomposition facilitates in situ oxygen scavenging.
The processing route controls retained oxygen at approximately 1.0 wt.%.
Approximately 1.0 wt.% interstitial oxygen strengthens HfNbTaTiZr.
Water quenching from 1500°C suppresses formation of alpha-HCP phases.
Suppressing alpha-HCP formation stabilizes a metastable beta-BCC structure.
Alpha-HCP phases in this alloy are embrittling.
A subsequent silicide coating forms a self-healing (Zr,Hf)O2 layer.
The self-healing (Zr,Hf)O2 layer improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The treated alloy will be nearly fully dense.
The treated alloy will have a metastable single beta-BCC phase.
The treated alloy will have superior high-temperature compression strength relative to cast or uncoated sintered baselines.
The treated alloy will have a significantly lower oxidation rate than cast or uncoated sintered baselines.
The baseline oxidation rate is approximately 570 mg² cm⁻⁴ h⁻¹.
Cast HfNbTaTiZr and uncoated sintered HfNbTaTiZr are susceptible to cracking, alpha-HCP embrittlement, and rapid oxidation.
Deviations from approximately 1.0 wt.% oxygen or the specified thermal processing may produce mixed alpha-plus-beta phases or insufficient densification.
The processed alloy is expected to have a grain size of approximately 33 µm.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies de-binding in flowing hydrogen followed by vacuum sintering, whereas the conditions describe sintering at 1400°C simultaneously in a hydrogen environment and at vacuum below 3×10⁻⁶ torr.

The mechanism relies on a subsequent silicide coating and its protective oxide, but no silicide-coating step is included in the stated intervention; the predicted outcome therefore conflates the specified uncoated processing route with an additional coating treatment.

The experiment proposes oxidation testing under the same vacuum conditions, even though the claimed outcome is high-temperature oxygen resistance; no oxygen partial pressure, oxidizing atmosphere, test temperature, or exposure duration is defined.
